purpose: Sanitized StreamGenerate request structures, captured 2026-09-29 by a temporary probe in injected.js (KAN-195). No prompt text and no CSRF token: every string is {type,length}.
capture_method: console.log('PAYLOAD_PROBE '+JSON) in both the fetch and XHR interceptors, read from the page console via Kapture. The network API was not usable: the buffer holds dozens of analytics and asset requests per second.
findings: The endpoint is StreamGenerate over XHR, as KAN-182 recorded. batchexecute is used for the auxiliary RPCs, not for the prompt.
19 of 20 top-level fields are byte-identical in shape between two different conversations. Only field [3] differs, and only in length (2488 vs 1657) — it is the conversation context blob.
The slot ARCHITECTURE.md calls the r_… session token, [0][2][0][0][3], is a ZERO-LENGTH string in BOTH samples. It is not a varying token.

CRITICAL: sample B came back UNGROUNDED with a structure identical to the grounded sample A. Request shape therefore does not determine whether the answer is grounded. Something outside the captured shape varies.

Consequently the premise in ARCHITECTURE.md — that ~40 dynamic inner fields including a per-attachment r_ token make the payload underivable — is NOT supported by these two samples. The structure is far more stable than that.
what_is_still_missing: A control sample from a request with NO notebook attached. The ping run did not produce one: it emitted only BatchExecute probes with hasEnvelope:false and never went through the typing path, so it is not a usable control.

Content-level data. Lengths alone cannot identify which field carries the notebook, because two different values can share a length. This is the hard limit of a sanitized capture — and it is why A and B being the same shape proves nothing about where the notebook lives.
A sample from a run that grounds in a NEW conversation, to see whether the ungrounded outcome in B is about conversation age rather than the payload.
next_experiment: Re-run horo_consult in a fresh conversation until it grounds, then diff that grounded sample against these two. If a grounded fresh conversation still matches B exactly, the difference is not in the payload at all.
